claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

Great! To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to start by understanding the ages of your children.

**What is the age of your child (or the youngest child if you have multiple)?**

Please tell me:
- Are they **under 16**, **16 to 19**, or **20 or older**?

This will help me determine which eligibility rules apply to your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, I have one child - Alex, who is 17 years old. I'm wanting to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thanks for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 17 years old. That means we need to check the rules for 16-19 year olds.

Let me navigate to the next part of the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to find out about Alex's current status. For 16-19 year olds, Child Benefit eligibility depends on whether they're in education or training.

**Is Alex currently:**

1. **In education or training** (e.g., school, college, university, approved training scheme)?
2. **Recently left education** (within the last 20 weeks)?
3. **Neither** - not in education or training and has been out for more than 20 weeks?

Which of these best describes Alex's situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex isn't in any education or training at the moment. He left school a while back - more than 20 weeks ago now.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for clarifying. Since Alex left school more than 20 weeks ago and isn't currently in education or training, let me navigate to the next step.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the assessment, I'm afraid I have to deliver an ineligible outcome for Alex.

## Result: **INELIGIBLE**

**Reason:**
Alex is 17 years old and is not currently in approved education or training. For 16-19 year olds to qualify for Child Benefit, they must be in one of the following:
- Full-time education (school, college, university)
- An approved training scheme
- Or if they've just left education, they can get a 20-week extension if they register with the careers service or armed forces

Since Alex left school more than 20 weeks ago and is not currently in any education or training programme, he no longer qualifies as a "qualifying child" for Child Benefit purposes.

**Important note:** If Alex were to enter approved education or training in the future, you could potentially reclaim Child Benefit at that point. It may be worth exploring whether he'd be interested in any training opportunities, apprenticeships, or further education that would make him eligible again.

Let me now provide you with your final eligibility determination:
